heading: INT. LITTLE LEAGUE DUGOUT - RAIN - DUSK

units.text: INT. LITTLE LEAGUE DUGOUT - RAIN - DUSK
A concrete bunker with a plank bench.
Rain ropes off the tin roof.
The scoreboard outside reads 14 to 2, bottom of the sixth.
Wet jerseys.
Silence.
COACH ROSCOE FINN, 60, hunched under a ball cap, studies his clipboard as if it will change the score.
PIA, 11, the catcher, picks at a strap on her shin guard.
LEVI, 10, stares at his glove.
TAMSIN, 12, the shortstop, kicks at a puddle forming at her cleats.
OTIS, 9, the smallest, sits at the end of the bench with a bat across his lap, his mouth working with a sentence he hasn't dared to say.
All right, listen up. One more inning. Doesn't matter what the board says.
units.name: ROSCOE

units.text: Nobody looks up.
Rain pounds.
Tams, you've got a good arm. Use it.
units.name: ROSCOE

units.text: Yes, Coach.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: Fourteen to two. Lord.
units.name: ROSCOE

units.text: Coach?
units.name: OTIS

units.text: Yeah, Otis.
units.name: ROSCOE

units.text: Can we just play it out?
units.name: OTIS

units.text: Roscoe looks at him for a long moment.
The kids go still.
He lowers the clipboard onto the bench.
Yeah, bud. We can do that.
units.name: ROSCOE

units.text: He stands, slaps the roof of the dugout twice with the flat of his hand.
Pia puts on her mask.
Levi pulls his glove on.
Tamsin lifts her head.
Otis grips the bat, stands, and walks out into the rain.
